WOODWORK — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: WOODWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Project activity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Project activity.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project activity.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project activity.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project activity.

2. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Information and Communication Technology
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

3. When learning Trends in woodwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Trends in woodwork.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Trends in woodwork.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Trends in woodwork.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Trends in woodwork.

4. When learning Portable Power Tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Portable Power Tools.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Portable Power Tools.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Portable Power Tools.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Portable Power Tools.

5. When learning Timber Defects, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Timber Defects.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Timber Defects.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber Defects.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Timber Defects.

6. When learning Mass Production, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Mass Production.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Mass Production.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Mass Production.

7. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Monitor
   B. Keyboard
   C. CPU
   D. Speaker

8. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Remove all guards

9. When learning Finishing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Finishing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Finishing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Finishing.

10. When learning Health and Safety in the Workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Health and Safety in the Workshop.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.

11. When learning Manufactured boards, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Manufactured boards.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Manufactured boards.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Manufactured boards.

12. When learning Detailed drawing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Detailed drawing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Detailed drawing.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Detailed drawing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Timber Defects and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Manufactured boards and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Mass Production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Finishing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project activity.

2. A — Information and Communication Technology

3. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Trends in woodwork.

4. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Portable Power Tools.

5. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Timber Defects.

6. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Mass Production.

7. C — CPU

8. B — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

9. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Finishing.

10. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Health and Safety in the Workshop.

11. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Manufactured boards.

12. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Detailed drawing.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Timber Defects; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)

16. (4 marks)
